title: Is DRAM also moving from planar to 3D? Samsung and SK Hynix are taking the lead, and the next wave of equipment demand is emerging
gist: With planar DRAM shrink hitting cost and difficulty limits, Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron are all pivoting to 3D stacked DRAM, and AMD has shown an experimental hybrid-bonded 3D DRAM architecture claiming up to 17x better energy efficiency than conventional HBM stacks. The shift moves DRAM competition from lithographic shrink to stack height at acceptable yield, heat and power, and redirects equipment demand toward etch, deposition, wafer grinding and hybrid bonding.

insights.claim: DRAM capacity growth has historically come from shrinking the process to pack more memory cells into the same die area, but as feature sizes shrink, manufacturing difficulty and cost rise rapidly and the room for growth from planar miniaturization alone is increasingly limited.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: The end of cheap planar shrinks forces a capex-heavy architectural transition across the entire memory industry.
insights.quote: as the size becomes smaller, manufacturing difficulty and costs rapidly increase, and the space for growth through flat miniaturization alone is becoming increasingly limited

insights.claim: Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Micron Technology have all begun exploring stacking DRAM upward instead of making DRAM cells smaller.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: All three surviving DRAM makers moving in the same direction makes 3D DRAM a sector-wide capex theme rather than a single-vendor experiment.
insights.locator: paragraph naming Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron

themes.theme: AMD hybrid-bonded 3D DRAM and AI energy efficiency

insights.claim: AMD unveiled an experimental 3D DRAM architecture that uses hybrid bonding to shorten the distance between memory and processors, claiming up to 17 times higher energy efficiency than traditional HBM stacks.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A 17x efficiency claim, if it productizes, would threaten the HBM franchise that currently drives SK Hynix and Samsung memory profits.
insights.quote: AMD (AMD-US) recently unveiled a 3D DRAM experimental architecture that uses hybrid bonding technology to shorten the distance between memory and processors

insights.claim: AI computing requires frequent transfer of large amounts of data between processors and memory, and the farther data moves the more power it consumes, so stacking DRAM directly on top of processors could improve transfer efficiency and cut power at the same time.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Data-movement energy, not compute, is becoming the binding constraint in AI systems, which shifts value toward memory-logic integration.
insights.quote: AI computing requires frequent transfer of large amounts of data between processors and memory, and the farther the data is moved, the more power is consumed.

insights.claim: Samsung is developing a vertical DRAM structure and has already implemented a 16-layer 3D DRAM stack internally.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A working 16-layer internal stack suggests 3D DRAM is closer to a manufacturable roadmap item than a research curiosity.
insights.quote: Samsung is developing a vertical DRAM structure and has already implemented a 16-layer 3D DRAM stack internally.

insights.claim: Samsung's plan is to manufacture memory and peripheral circuits separately and then integrate them through hybrid bonding.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Splitting array and periphery wafers creates new demand for wafer-to-wafer bonding and thinning tools per DRAM bit.

insights.claim: SK Hynix has designated 3D DRAM as a key development direction for DRAM below 10 nanometers and has invested in related engineering talent and technology R&D.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: 3D is being positioned as the successor path once sub-10nm planar DRAM stalls, framing SK Hynix's late-decade capex.

insights.claim: Micron was earlier than its rivals in patent positioning, having accumulated over 30 3D DRAM-related patents as of August 2022.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Early IP depth could give Micron leverage or freedom-to-operate advantages as the industry converges on 3D DRAM.
insights.quote: Micron was even earlier in its patent layout, having accumulated over 30 3D DRAM-related patents as of August 2022.

themes.theme: New basis of competition in memory

insights.claim: The basis of DRAM competition may shift from who can shrink the process the most to who can stack DRAM highest while maintaining yield, heat dissipation and power consumption.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Competitive ranking in memory could reshuffle, because stacking, bonding and thermal skills differ from lithographic shrink skills.
insights.quote: in the future, they may further compare who can stack DRAM higher while maintaining yield, heat dissipation, and power consumption

insights.claim: Simultaneous investment by the major memory manufacturers in 3D DRAM reflects that the way the DRAM industry competes is itself changing, not merely that a new process option exists.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Structural change in the competitive metric usually precedes market-share shifts and margin dispersion.

insights.claim: As DRAM moves vertically, chips require deeper and more complex internal structures to be etched precisely and different wafers to be stacked and connected flat, changing what memory manufacturing equipment must do.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Process-step mix shifts spending away from pure patterning toward deposition, etch and bonding intensity per wafer.

insights.claim: Beyond exposure equipment, the importance of etching, thin film deposition, wafer grinding and hybrid bonding tools may gradually increase as 3D DRAM ramps.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Etch, deposition, grinding and bonding equipment vendors gain share of memory capex relative to lithography suppliers.
insights.quote: besides exposure equipment, the importance of equipment such as etching, thin film deposition, wafer grinding, and hybrid bonding may gradually increase
